html:
The Korean kingdom of Silla in the years from 668 to 935, after it had conquered its rivals and ruled most of the Korean peninsula. Its capital was Gyeongju, in the southeast.

Silla began as the weakest of the Three Kingdoms. It allied with the Tang dynasty of China, and together they destroyed Baekje in 660 and Goguryeo in 668. The Tang then tried to rule the peninsula itself. Silla fought them from 670 to 676 and drove them out north of the Taedong River. The far north and Manchuria went to Balhae, a state founded by former Goguryeo people, so historians also call this the Northern and Southern States period.

Unified Silla was a high point of Korean Buddhist art:

  • The temple of Bulguksa and the Seokguram grotto near Gyeongju.
  • The Cheomseongdae observatory, from the earlier Silla period.
  • Monks and students travelled to Tang China, and Korean merchants traded across the Yellow Sea.

Society was ruled by a rigid "bone rank" system that fixed what office a person could hold by birth. In the 9th century the aristocracy fought over the throne, provincial lords grew strong, and rebels set up rival kingdoms. In 935 the last king, Gyeongsun, gave up his realm to Goryeo, which soon reunited the peninsula.
sum: The Korean kingdom of Silla in the years from 668 to 935, after it had conquered its rivals and ruled most of the Korean peninsula. Its capital was Gyeongju, in the southeast.
